[h1]一份游戏 三倍享受[/h1] 这是款可以同时操控三个角色并搭配三个卡组进行战斗的暗黑赛博风卡牌游戏。剧情啥的可有可无，反抗军VS黑恶势力的老套路。而在核心的战斗体验上，操控数量的改变也确实为游戏带来了策略性和构筑方面的增强。局内战斗通过各自角色自身的定位及专属卡组，可以相辅相成、合一二战。各式各样功能的卡牌中也有一些相当富有创意的机制词条。角色还可以搭配特殊器官以及局外天赋系统进行加强，可重复游戏度也很高。 [h1]出牌 出牌 再出牌[/h1] 说实话卡牌肉鸽游戏这个市场，在如今已然是泛滥成灾的红海，同质化可谓相当严重。不过本作却多少给我一种耳目一新的感觉，这当然主要得益于它主打的三角色同战系统。简单来说有3个职业大类9名不同的角色，如果简单粗暴的理解的话：卫士相当于T，主打防御；突击兵是DPS，擅长直接攻击；专家则偏向于辅助，可以通过增益Buff或召唤等方式间接左右战局。 我们战斗的时候采用敌我上下分屏的方式作战，我方的每一名角色都有独立的主动技能、AP（行动点）和卡组（专属卡+通用卡）。由于也没有出牌顺序，角色之间是完全平行的关系，要结束就全队结束，这就使得我们可以在策略上大作文章。 比方说，战局开始时你别急着让DPS输出，而是应该纵览下全队卡牌状态。万一专家组的成员有个削减敌方护甲或是给全队增加攻击的BUFF，那必须要让专家出牌以获得最强的输出能力。而且技能的释放也十分讲究，不能没有CD就无脑放，还是需要根据战场形式灵活处理。例如嘲讽技能，如果敌方的意图本身就不在你的队友就完全没必要释放，要在关键时刻护住全队。 游戏还有着相当繁多的机制标签，乍一看名称你甚至无法直观理解是什么意思。而有一些标签在其它游戏中倒也不是很常见，这里就随便举些例子 。爆炸：单位死亡后如果其它单位没有护盾便会受到伤害。这玩意最屌的是AOE+不分敌我，运用时机得当的话真的是相当牛逼。透支：可以跨回合借AP以增强单回合的出牌效果（非常适合一波流或消灭指定的强力敌人）。傲气：攻击增强，但是被打就消失（跟气球一样泄气了）。此外还有交战、硬化、迷茫等数十种奇怪的效果，还有布置机制，能召唤多样化的额外单位。 [h1]总结[/h1] 画面炫酷也饶有特色的打牌游戏，BOSS设计也十分出彩。不过局外成长资源给的比较抠，建议再大方亿点点。 [quote] 游玩百态，将游玩心得用汉语化作玩家的指明灯，(๑•̀ㅂ•́)و✧ [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35402408/]点击这里关注汉化语录~[/url] 如果喜欢这个评测，请点个赞让更多人看见 [/quote]

Solid game. Lots of fun, especially for the price. It is a bit easy, and that's my only real criticism. I've gotten to the upper complexity runs, and I think I need to shift my view of the goal of the game has shifted from 'try to win' to 'try to get a perfect win in every battle.' That's definitely doable with any combination of characters, but doubly so for the middle selection for each class. Rook can win the game on her own without ever letting an enemy take a turn in every battle except one, against enemies which can't be targeted by cards- but that really only means the tank has to do something instead of stand around being gorgeously rendered in 3d. The middle tank (is it Rejj? I forget) who boosts armor instead of block is a standout upgrade over the Paladin, as he doubles as a possible damage dealer and his taunts are more reliable. A possible exception is the tinker vs the holo summoner- both of those are really good. The third slot characters are just okay. Aleph, the sniper, is really cool in terms of design, but you end up waiting a long time to charge up a big move. The samurai gunman is also cool in terms of design, but he isn't really powerful. Aleph is a better gunner. Rook is a better striker. The third slot tank wants to take damage, and while that can be fine, I don't love it. That last bit is just some personal preference. There's also a bit of skew in the usefulness of cards. Gambit, a card which lets you discard your hand and draw 4 more, is the only thing I think I'd ever keep in my failsafe slots. Six copies, straight up, and I'd never regret putting them there. Every character wants two copies of that card. On the other hand, a card that might be more exciting, like 'Big ol' Rocket launcher,' will only ever see use in niche builds relying on deploying characters (there is one which reduces the AP cost of cards in hand to zero, giving incentive for big cards) or a slightly worse build that gives offensive gear cards Flurry, giving you a 50% chance to get them back and reduce their cost to zero. Admittedly, a super cool design for an augment, but there are plenty of other more stable routes to victory. There are some bugs. Draft mode sometimes displays the wrong card. You select the card you want then find you received a completely different one. The game sometimes doesn't update character attributes accurately the round that they change, but that doesn't happen often. I'm confident the technical issues will be fixed in a timely fashion. Playing with the builds is exceptionally fun. I really like to tinker once I get a few augments. It has a good gameplay loop, well-designed enemies, killer vibes. I'd recommend it now, in its current state, but I expect that once a few more rounds of refinement are finished up this will be a real gem.

[h1]《零异机动队》简评[/h1] [h1]特殊的闯关地图模式[/h1] 本作的闯关模式比较特殊，采用的是一种网状节点线路图的形式，即用路线将地图上的一个个行动节点（房间）连接起来，玩家在各个节点之间移动，触发新抵达节点的内容。这些节点主要包括三大类——战斗、商店（商社代理）和随机事件。战斗房间，包括普通战斗、精英敌人战斗和最终Boss战斗，战斗胜利，获得金币、卡牌等奖励。商店房间，消耗金币，恢复HP、补充补给，或者获取和升级卡牌。随机事件，触发随机遭遇事件，可能会带来正面或负面效果。 本作和其它卡牌游戏不同，并没有借鉴爬塔的闯关地图模式，其不同之处在于，玩家可以通过连接路线，任意行动到相邻的节点，并非只能向前不能退后。因此，一张地图上的所有节点，理论上是可以全部走完的。只不过又涉及到节点移动的另一项内容——补给点数。玩家向一个未探索的节点移动，便会消耗1点补给。补给消耗殆尽，玩家仍然可以继续探索地图，只不过但战斗奖励会减少，并且玩家在补给不为0的情况下撤离，还会获得额外奖励。（PS：补给点数还可以是负数。）因此，如何规划既有的路线进行探索，以及补给的消耗和收益最大化的问题，也是玩家战斗过程中需要注意的一环。 [h1]有趣的卡牌战斗方式[/h1] 本作的基础胜负规则，有些类似于《游戏王》的战斗怪兽卡，但也有所不同。玩家在游戏之初，选择三名小队成员，便是玩家最基础的角色牌（可以理解为战斗怪兽卡），并且在游戏的卡牌对战开始之后，我方小队成员的角色牌和敌方所有参战单位，按照次序直接放置于战场之上对立。位于场上的敌我双方的角色牌（包括我方打出手牌，召唤出来的其它作战单位卡牌），牌面内容包括被动技能、主动技能、攻击力、格挡值、血量值等。角色牌的战斗过程很简单，选择对面的敌方单位发起进攻，攻击一次后角色进入到疲惫状态无法继续攻击，所有操作完事，选择回合结束，开始进入敌人的自动攻击阶段。战斗胜利/失败的规则，即一方场上所有的角色牌血量归零即可。 上述的三张角色牌，并非参与到卡组构筑之中，游戏中还有独立的卡组构筑体系，用以辅助三张角色牌的战斗。玩家消耗一定数值的角色能量，将该角色对应卡组的手牌打出，根据出牌的词条效果，达到输出、增益、恢复、援助等各种作用，这一点和常规卡牌一样。只不过在这款游戏中，玩家的卡组不再是传统的单兵作战的一副卡组，转而改变为一个小队三名角色各自拥有一副卡组，且每一个小队角色的卡组所出牌消耗的能量并不通用。 [h1]角色搭配和战力养成[/h1] 一局游戏中，玩家的小队角色有三名。目前，可供玩家选择的角色共有九名（初始三名角色，后续六名角色需要完成成就解锁）。卫士三人——老兵战将、佣兵队长神怪、赛博无序者骚乱，突击兵三人——暴徒枪手叛将、企业杀手乌鸦、杀戮机器提丰，专家三人——全息神童幻影、主工程师铸补匠、强化狙击手阿列夫零。不同的角色，拥有不同的主动/被动技能以及不同的卡组。如何搭配这些角色进行组队，这也是一个策略内容。 其次，在游戏中，角色的战力提升是有多个方面共同组成的，并非不断扩充卡组实现构筑这一种途径。第一，小队三名成员各自卡组的构筑体系逐步成型；第二，奖励获得的装备（类似于圣物这种），根据装备词条，穿戴在合适的成员身上；第三，消耗合成记忆体对角色的特定卡牌升级，减少消耗、改变词条等。只有这三个方向共同提升，且小队三名成员均衡发展，才能在愈来愈强的地图战斗中，一点点站稳获得战斗胜利。 [h1]构筑体系的优缺利弊[/h1] 根据上述的内容，本作的卡牌对战的构筑策略，其实包含了很多个方面。最主要的内容包括以下几点：小队角色的组队选择，随机装备的获取穿戴，（专属）卡牌的升级方向，角色卡组的各自构筑，卡组之间的战斗关联……因此，本组的卡牌对战构筑策略的要素其实是很丰富也很完善的，玩家玩起的确有新颖和特色之处，并且熟练精深了规则玩法，有了自己的策略构思之后，玩起来确实很痛快。 不过，也正是因为如此，导致了游戏很复杂，新人玩家初上手时候，真不一定能够适应游戏的难度设计，甚至在新手阶段，会有一种为了高难度而强行提升难度的感觉。例如，第一次战斗，打通了第一个地图进入到第二个地图区域，面临的第一场普通战斗，就直接让本人懵圈了，敌方三个小怪的被动属性为攻击附带燃烧，然后三个小怪一轮共计下来，叠加的燃烧数值能够达到十来点，直接让我方一名角色从满血进入到残血，所有角色扛不住两个回合，甚至有个血少一点的角色一个回合就给干没血了，关键是这三个小怪血量还不低，通过燃烧硬生生的把我方全员给干废。这样的情况在游戏中其实很常见，因此，游戏真的需要调整一下难度设计的增长梯度，让新人玩家有一个好的开始，而不是一上来就是高难度。 [h1]最后[/h1] 《零异机动队》这款卡牌对战游戏，在未来科幻的赛博世界中，以其新颖独特的卡牌对战玩法，搭配科幻感十足的美术风格、UI页面和背景音乐，让玩家享受到一场不一样的卡牌对战游戏。这款游戏规则有些复杂，上手到深入有一定的难度，但是玩家精通之后，就能发现本作的魅力所在。喜欢卡牌对战的玩家，不妨试一试本作，很有特色的。 [quote]关注[url= https://store.steampowered.com/curator/36224058/]老实人鉴赏家 [/url] [url= https://steamcommunity.com/groups/laoshirenLSR]老实人评测[/url]：独立游戏爱好者聚集地，黄油绅士交流中心。 不错过游戏的亮点，不放过游戏的槽点，带给玩家最直观的测评感受。[/quote]

I enjoyed it. I'd recommend it with one caveat: It's *mind-numbingly* easy. This might be the easiest Deckbuilder since Mahokenshi. There's a lot of degenerate combos and a lot of just incredibly powerful abilities, and the Failsafe system makes those degenerate combos consistent between runs. This game needs a *lot* of balance changes. Even on Max difficulty with all the modifiers turned on, it's easy to build your operators and your deck so that every combat ends on turn 1 before the enemies attack. It took about 16-17 hours to climb the difficulty chain, then I did one more run with all of the difficulty modifiers on and still didn't take any damage the entire run. Another few runs for the interesting achievements (3 of class type), and that was it. I'm not sure why my playtime is showing 13.4, it's about 20. I had an all-day internet outage yesterday and that's probably the cause of it. That being said, I actually really like the game design and I had fun while playing it. The closest comparison game is Arcanium: Rise of Akhan, which is in my top 5 deckbuilders of all time.

After sitting on it for a few days I've decided to bitterly change this review to negative. Here's the thing; the games balance is so out of wack I don't want to keep playing. Yes, I got my money's worth. But hearing the devs talk in the forums about making any change besides balancing the overpowered characters demonstrates a gross misunderstanding of what makes deckbuilders fun for people like me. TLDR one of the characters starting decks can solo the hardest difficulty without help from their allies. This is not acceptable design and should be hotfixed before any other changes. The fun of deckbuilders is building the deck. Being handed a solution from the getgo begs the question; why play? Answer, I stopped playing after unlocking that character. I will check back when updates come and will certainly update this review if I put more hours into the game. Bellow is my original positive review -- It was fun. If you like deck builders you’ll get your moneys worth. The game doesn’t have the same replay ability as the best of the genre. It’s a bit too easy to go infinite and the hero balance is quite off. I wrote this review shortly after finishing the last “ascension” and I left it on since buying it. I do love the aesthetic and quite enjoy the few bits of lore (I’m also a sucker for cyberpunk). The first few times you pop off with Renegade or Rook is quite fun. Honestly, the general party chemistry of Renegade and Paladin felt unique in the growing sub genre of party based deckbuilders. So yeah, cool game. About 24 hours of content. That’s probably worth 10$ isn’t it? About the price of a movie ticket. Plus, the devs are responsive and say they plan to address the balance so maaaaaaayhe it is the next great deckbuilder by the time you’re reading this.

游戏是好游戏，可以玩，但是别选乌鸦！别选乌鸦！别算乌鸦！ 一个本可以九分的游戏，被屎一样的操作机制给折半，纵观市面上大大小小的各种打牌游戏，这个游戏是独一份的需要点好几下才能执行操作的，用牌攻击敌人，得先选中卡牌，再点击敌人，（增益队友同理）接着还要等待相当缓慢的步骤结算，比如攻击后的敌我双方增益建议效果，它不是实时变化的，而是需要时间进行反馈（可能在一到两秒），无法像杀戮尖塔那样可以拖动卡牌到单位上直接进行选中。游戏初期其实还好，但在使用乌鸦之后这种吃屎的感觉达到了顶峰，刷牌就得刷半天。 乌鸦也是这个游戏的机制漏洞，如果要玩这个游戏只能劝各位别碰乌鸦，严重超模。她已经超脱了轮椅的概念，不是强不强的问题了，目前打到副总裁，没有失败过一次，乌鸦可以做到不靠任何游戏内新增卡牌，任何强化，任何buff，任何队友，单人无伤通关boss。这个角色直接就让所谓的rogue变成了笑话，因为只要在失忆那里固定好卡后就能一路杀穿，目前我能想到的可以克制乌鸦的只有反伤和限制出牌次数，但这两个debuff还没看到过。（两张强化制定战略，两张强化冲刺，一张任意一费抽牌，替换掉乌鸦的非专业卡，手牌速满十张，九张牌固定不动，7张低费卡循环刷牌。左脚踩右脚螺旋升天，都不用管敌人机制的。建议游戏改名乌鸦机动队） 最后就是即使没有乌鸦，前期的难度也过于简单，不明白为什么设这么多关。 希望制作组能把打牌的体验提升下，我一开始还以为是自己的问题，游戏里的那个快速出牌没有生效，去b站上找游戏视频，发现大家都是吃相同的屎，释然了。

玩了半天的感受是场外奖励极低，场外成长也不多。虽然看似是控制三个人物对应的三套卡牌，但是通用卡牌过多，大家有很多相同的牌型，不像其他同类型游戏换个角色玩法就大相径庭也没有相同的牌，这样感觉同时控制三个角色其实噱头大于玩法。而且初期局内奖励的卡牌大部分都是对应的后期解锁的人物，没办法很好的融入初期角色的牌库，比如一堆格斗射击制造之类的卡牌初期三人组基本就很难使用。所以初期角色装备收益明显大于新卡牌，导致初期体验极差，反正我是没耐心继续玩下去了。

今年的卡牌肉鸽游戏简直爆发式的扎堆推出，并且基本上都有很强的《杀戮尖塔》的影子，也就是改改卡面和效果，然后就做成了一款新的东西。讲道理，玩的多了也有一些免疫了。所以我在刚接触《零异机动队》这款游戏的时候是并没有保持什么太高的期待的。赛博朋克的故事背景，卡牌构筑爬塔式的核心方法，加上一些肉鸽元素，商业页面简单的介绍并不能激发我任何兴趣。然而当我真正入手这款游戏的时候，我发现事情并没有那么简单，游戏在很多层面上进行了大胆的创新，并带给玩家强烈的新鲜感，以及并非传统的打牌套路。 [h1]略显俗套的剧情[/h1] 本作游戏的剧情故事属于烂大街的赛博朋克故事，故事的舞台设定在泽祖拉，这是一座曾经繁盛的庞大都市，但在一场世界大战中几近全毁，因滥用人工通用智能（AGI）而酿成了恶果。泽祖拉被认为是仅存的AGI数据中心所在地，周围由各托拉斯围建起禁区，对外宣称是为了保护公众不受失控的AGI影响，实际上是为了控制泽祖拉的科技遗产。而玩家是扮演反抗军中的一员，对抗引发世界大战的各方势力，并寻找城市秘密的真相。 [h1]三个女人一台戏[/h1] 本作最吸引我的地方，在于游戏并非像传统卡牌游戏一样，进行单兵作战，而是需要玩家调配三个单位进入卡牌战斗，有负责输出的DPS，有负责防御吸引火力的T，以及一名加持buff的辅助。游戏中共有九名可选择的人物，每个人物都有独特的技能和专属卡牌，而每个人物也独立一套卡牌以及出牌点数。游戏中卡牌的类型有通用卡牌与职业卡牌，卡牌之间相互独立又相互关联。尤其是各个职业之间的搭配，更是游戏的一绝。并且当玩家赢得一场战斗后，可以获得更多的卡牌来更新自己的卡组。三个单位的卡组需要相互协调，这就使得卡牌构筑是相当的烧脑。在出牌阶段，因为三个单位的卡牌相互独立，玩家也需要选择卡牌打出的优先级。有可能在手上没有输出牌的情况下使用辅助的最后一点打出抽牌就可以获得一张惊喜的输出牌来直接赢得胜利。卡面上包含的是传统卡牌游戏的攻击力和生命值显示，并且每个角色都有独特的技能，也包括敌人。所以玩家需要在战斗中看好每一名角色的技能是什么。 [h1]创新型的肉鸽[/h1] 本作在关卡大地图中采用了传统肉鸽的形式，但是大胆的进行了一定的创新。在传统的爬塔游戏中，玩家只能一直向前，没有回头路可选。而本作玩家则拥有回头路的机会，甚至玩家只要规划好，便可以把整张地图全部探索掉。游戏中每次移动都会消耗补给，而部分事件还会额外消耗补给，但是在一些特定的地点也会有补给的奖励。游戏毫不吝啬地图上探索的奖励以及事件的奖励，玩家可以快速积累前期的财富，并在前期可以通过战斗获得大量的额外卡牌来填充自己的卡组，自由度相当高。 [h1]角色的成长[/h1] 卡牌爬塔这个赛道现在已经非常拥挤了，只有创新才能在众多游戏中脱颖而出。本作游戏中不仅玩家需要派出三名单位一起参与战斗，还需要同时对他们进行成长管理。消耗对局中的合成记忆体，来学习每个人物不同的天赋技能。并且需要在探索过程中发现各种各样的装备来装备到不同的人物身上，从而提升他们本身的属性。 [table][td][b]欢迎关注我们 [/b][url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/10591434/]突突突发糖辣！[/url] [/td][/table]

[h1] A Card Game KING review [/h1] Zero Division has rather standard roguelike deckbuilder with a lot of the basics down, but it does have its share of shortcomings (more on that later). Despite that, the card play is fun, each character (you bring 3 to each mission) feels distinct enough and the enemy design/variety is pretty good. The game also gives you a lot of flexibility with choices. When you choose new cards you choose from 6 cards, when getting equipment, you choose from 2, shops have a lot of things to spend money on and you can end a level earlier if you want. I really enjoyed the extra control that most games have restricted. Deckbuilding is also fun since you have 3 agents to control, each with a special passive and starting cards, but the rest of the deck is made using a shared pool of cards that adds additional freedom and variety. The game does have a rather significant drawback as I mentioned earlier. And that's that over the course of few hours, you've would have seen most of the cards in the game. That's a shame because the underlying mechanics are great but it feels like the content is not big enough to support its longevity. To be fair, the game is priced well for it's content size, but the problem is that some of the extra content is very slow to unlock and by that point fatigue can set in as you play the same combos over and over again. It doesn't help that the difficulty options are also unlocked through the same system, slowly, which can be a problem for experienced gamers that found the beginning difficulty too easy. To make it worse, some agents are locked behind those difficulty levels, losing on versatility in agent selection during the early game. Draft mode is similarly only unlocked at later levels. I do think there is more good and bad, and is ultimately worth playing, but be aware that the progress can be slow. [h1][b]The positive[/b] [/h1] + Solid gameplay. + Game gives you plenty of options on how to make your deck and equipment combo. + Good enemy variety and design. [h1][b]The neutral[/b][/h1] * Interface slows down the game. What I mean is that the time between getting rewards and getting into a new fight is longer than it needs to be. For example, when you get the reward like card or equipment, you get them to your vault. Then you have to go to your vault and open them one by one. Then choose the reward. Then assign the cards to each agent. The wait for the game to load. Games like Arcanium solved this by allowing to see the cards immediately and assign them to heroes instantly. Compared to games like StS that feel very snappy, Zero Division feels encumbered by unnecessary slew of extra clicks. [h1][b]The negative[/b][/h1] - Burst of fun at the beginning but the content dries up after several hours. - Unlocking difficulty levels and agents is too slow. I was ready for greater challenges hours ago :(. Fun modes, like draft are also locked behind the grind. - Some balance of cards isn't great. There are a lot of cards that are simply bad. There is a 3 cost card (you get 3 actions per turn) that does 10 damage. You have combos that do much more damage than that so spending your whole turn on measly 10 damage is never worth it. [h1][b]Conclusion:[/b] [/h1] Despite its shortcomings, the good outweighs the bad, and the game delivers a fun cyberpunk themed burst of fun, before inevitably running our of new things to try. Recommended. Decent deckbuilder roguelike that suffers from poor balance. The game essentially has a sideboard mechanic where you can bring cards from previous runs into future runs, but as is this completely trivialises the game. The renegade can go infinite without any real effort, and only gets more broken as you unlock talents on her. Can see some cool concepts with the modifiers for challenge runs are interesting, with pretty much all of them being double-edged swords that you can play around, but tbh you can just slap every modifier on and the game plays almost identically as it did when you first started. My first challenge run was one with every modifier [CR50] - and was over in the space of about 15 minutes. The game is polished in most other aspects, and while I can't recommend this to others at the moment, I am keen to check back in in future and see what Robot Cat have done with the game.

If this was early access, I'd say I'm excited to see the full release, it looks promising so far. But it's a full release, I've had to double check, I didn't believe it. The game has everything but instead of the ideas being pulled into a tightly knit gameplay, it boils like a goulash made out of rotten meat and you're sweating like a pig just inhaling that acursed boil. It is the most obvious case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde. Lemme explain: Graphics Love the cyberpunk idea. It is your standard CP - you have runners, mutants, wild AI, synthetics, corporations, megabuildings, it is classic CP, solid if formulaic, although very refreshing to see in a digital card game. That's for aesthetics, however the graphic execution is all over the place. You have working animated bosses, yet each arena is a hodge-podge of basic shapes (alright buldings, but they look like Lego blocks drenched in Primalex painting). Operators have a clean and well-executed visual appereance, yet cards featuring them have a distincting anime aesthetic and you can clearly see that some cards were generated/created through different seed. As far as I know, there was AI generation involved, which is ok, but you can really see the similarities between card art here and myriads of generative manga on DeviantArt. That is not how you want to integrate AI into your work. Mythgard might be dead, but the game still has a kickass art that should be an inspiration for many more, especially because Mythgard melds multiple genres well (thanks to cohesive art). Progression That one is just off up to a point of "Start over with QA". Navigating districts feels dull and boss battles having more and more stages the further I go do not feel rewarding, it's just a slog and oftentimes I decided to put my team out of misery by resigning before they die waiting for the next stage. The idea of phases is really good, but do not overdo it. I'd also probably make each district map more intricate and longer with shorter boss battles. I understand player can extract early, but it feels unintuitive and... let me ask: Player basically has the option to skip a district. Do you really want to encourage them to skip whole parts of core gameplay? Difficulty scaling is totally off. I have read in the reviews that for someone felt the game to be too easy. Well either developers patched the difficulty track or the player came upon some truly deranged combo, but I do not have patience for that. ADD hamster wants to go brrrrrm and dakka dakka right now. That being said some fights feel to easy or too hard and they usually go one after another. One difficulty over Meatsack is ten times harder, and you have like twelve more to go! Who tested this and said: Yep, mofos are gonna enjoy this bad boy. If you have so many difficulties you should ramp it up gradually. Unlocks are hidden behind some challenges, but most of them require you to beat higher difficulties. That is not good design decision. Players should be able to grind out the stuff to beat the difficulty they are stuck on, while nifty player get their stuff earlier thanks to beating the higher difficulties without needing to unlock more stuff (that can eventually help) and getting more XP - that way you encourage both groups to continue playing. Cards Where is your g*dd*mn library of cards and augmentations? Somebody forgot to implement it or was it a deliberate decision? I want to be able to check all the stuff I have unlocked, all the pretty stuff to look at, I want to sit at the table and theorycraft all the decks I could muster. But I can't, because there's no comprehensive library. Some keywords seem useless and some cards are totally unbalanced - either too good or d*mn expensive, further narrowing possible choices. Starter decks feel good at first, because they are fully capable of carrying you into many many fights, but that is the problem - your starter deck in Slay the Spire ain't basically flavorless because reasons, but because it is a base for you to build your own deck at the top of during the run. I was using Renegade on punch and puncher harder OTKs the whole time when I have noticed you can deck her out to do AMMO damage, but why would you? Her basic deck and abilities railroad you to do WHAM OTKs with fists, that's it. Gameplay There are a few bugs, but honestly - nothing gamebreaking, that's good. I only have problem with how GUI works for the player, that is - the little f*cker secretly works with your enemies to undermine you. You cannot properly zoom back to game board when fabricating cards (Hearthstone understands that you want your "strategical overview" when deciding what card to discover/fabricate to best suit your needs). Pick cards out of overcrowded hand is clunky at best (it is quite easy to pick a wrong card since the cursor detects one over another). Loading times are bit too long, or I should say - animated sequences? They just feel like overstaying a bit, in a card game you want to kapow fast. Failsafe (a carryover sideboard if you will) mechanic is neat, however it has one fatal flaw - you either collect cards for you future dream run or you just use the same cards all over again because they just compliment your working strategy. I understand the idea, but this was better done in Across the Obelisk - you can basically precraft your starting deck and play into your build by choosing the right path. In Zero Division there is nothing done beside failsafe, it is a weird mix of random and customized gameplay. It sounds like I ditched the game, but I really like it, I would play it more, but not with how it plays now. There are just too many hiccups along the road. I really wish it was still early access, because that would make me hopeful for a good release.

Do you like deck builders? Do you like cyberpunk? Do you like being called a meatbag and then injecting heavily sketchy technology directly into your frontal lobe in the middle of the night in a sketchy alley full of enemies? If so, Zero Division is for you! First off, this game is [i]very[/i] well designed. It's intentionally built to allow you to hit for insane combinations while also not making it mandatory to do so. The game [i]wants[/i] you to find devastating new ways to use your group, while also not punishing you for trying something new or less optimal. It's refreshing. To expand on the combo possibilities: Your base units deal about 2-3 damage on their own. Or, if you're clever, you can make that ~60 damage. The combos and supports available in the game can make a mean difference. Difficulty wise, it's both forgiving and challenging! Zero Division has hit that sweet point in balance where it's uncertain if you'll be victorious in almost every encounter, and yet you'll likely pull it off with zero losses. No fight is ever a cake walk, and yet every fight has a surprising margin of error built into it. Achievements are [b]achievable[/b] in this game! No 1000+ hours of grinding for a silly achievement, every achievement is an attainable challenge that is [i]fun[/i]. I really, really like how the challenges/achievements are done in this game and I hope it sets a precedent for other games to follow suit. Lastly, the design is also forgiving. Slay the Spire (another popular deckbuilding game) gives you one unit with three choice cards after every encounter - this can easily screw you over based on luck. Zero division instead distributes the load and reduces luck as a factor significantly. You are allowed a selection of multiple reward cards to choose from a large pool, you have three units under your command so if one goes down the other two are still able to keep swinging. This also helps make hard-counters less of a hard counter and more of a 'time to get creative' situation. Add into this the individuality of the units and their upgrades, and you have a skill-based deckbuilder. All in all, I do recommend it!

There's a good card game in here, but it's held back by a few issues for me. Something about the "physicality" of the cards doesn't feel right. Most cards require two clicks to play. Once to select and once to target. You can occasionally just drag a card from hand to target, but not always. It never seems intuitive to me when I am allowed or not to do this. This sounds trivial, but it is a constant annoyance. When I play a well made card game, I almost forget about the interface, and am thinking and acting on my ideas almost directly. But here, I am constantly distracted by having to fight just a little with the UI. There are on-hover visual effects on a lot of cards, but it often lags just a little bit. Not much, but just enough to make everything look sluggish and unresponsive. This is especially noticeable when an animation effect is in progress elsewhere on the screen. Probably related to the above: the game is extremely resource intensive. While some of the 3D scenes used are nice, it doesn't seem to warrant just how much this game gets the fans on my CPU spinning like no other game. I seriously cannot understand how this game chokes up so much resource. At the end of the day, it's just a card game, it shouldn't be resource intensive at all. I should add, this was even though I was running the game on "low" settings, and even though my PC has great specs. It's a card game with a lot of unlockables, but there is no where I can look up all cards. There are lots of keyword mechanics in this game, which are explained in popover tooltips when viewing a card, but no where I can just look up all status effects. I would expect any card game like this to have something like a "compendium" where I can see a list of keyword terms/mechanics, and a collection of all cards currently unlocked (and maybe a list of requirements to unlock additional cards). There are random event nodes with some little bit of event text and a decision. I can't quite put my finger on it, but they always feel like a totally random coin flip for something maybe positive or something maybe negative. But there's no sense of stake in the world. It's almost never clear to me why the decision I made was correct or incorrect. It's hard to explain, but the wording on card text always refers to your characters as "allies" and enemies as "enemies" _regardless of who's point of view it's coming from_. This is constantly confusing to me, because it is the opposite of how any other card game does it. To give an example, you might see an effect on an enemy. When you hover over it, it says "allies get +1 attack when this unit attacks". I will always read that as "the allies of the card with the effect", as opposed to what it actually means which is to always refer to the protagonists. This is a minor thing, but it constantly catches me out. Just another little thing that distracts me from enjoy what is probably a good card game.

So, this one flew under my radar until I randomly bought it with a couple of other Deckbuilders, haven't really touched the others yet because this game has sucked me in. The Combat can be very deep and that's nice, a lot of very different and interesting enemies with a TON of different buffs, debuffs, conditions always changing the way you play each fight, yet I've not really found a fight where I thought"this is unbeatable." even when I lost I realised my mistakes and when I fought the enemy again later I took it down, it's a phenomenal at rewarding you for your brain wrinkles working correctly. Auguments and different cards give you the ability to make every run, even those with the same characters, feel different and unique. I highly recommend this to pretty much anyone even passingly interested in deckbuilders.

Look, Zero Division is no Slay the Spire but I thoroughly enjoyed the artstyle and steampunky aesthetic. Despite it's shortcomings, it has one major thing going for it: It respects your time. After roughly 30 hours I 100%ed the game and did everything there is to do. Although this sounds like a downside at first, it's not. It's refreshing to play a roguelike, that you can actually finish and be done with. The feeling of closure with such games isn't always as easily achieved. The somewhat limited cardpool and mechanics and brevity of runs let you understand the game completely in just a couple of sessions. Also, it's nice that it doesn't feel artifically bloated and the challenges are actually doable. If you played a roguelike deckbuilder, Zero Division won't present you with anything drastically new. What I really enjoyed though, is, that the game is easily exploidable. With some basic knowledge of the core conecepts and the built in mechanic to keep cards and upgrades between runs, you can achieve very persistent decks - every run. In that regard, it plays more like a power fantasy than a grindfest. It's a short and nice experience. I liked it.

最近一直在摸鱼的时候玩的一款有一定肉鸽元素的打牌游戏。首先画风是偏写实的黑暗赛博朋克风格，很对我胃口。游戏的玩法基本规则并不复杂，攻击护甲伤害类型装备卡牌升级这些，但是需要一个人抓3副牌一起打，既增加了游戏的难度也增加了游戏的操作感。尤其是乌鸦或者叛将结合能过牌、回费、再动的卡牌，一回合内可以打出巨量的伤害，游戏的体验直接拉满。此外，我很喜欢游戏里“复杂度”的设定。“复杂度”是一个中性词，复杂度的上升并不意味着难度完全上升。事实上在前几个复杂度里很多操作都是只有在复杂度存在的情况下才能实现的，例如依靠自爆buff修血然后一回合内清理掉多个怪。因此复杂度的存在反而使得游戏的爽感更强了。目前而言我觉得游戏的内容还不是特别多吧，希望能快快推出新机制、新装备、新卡牌、新地图，虽然总体来说现在还是对得起价格的。另外叛将作为输出类角色是独一档的强，机制完美、卡牌联动好，希望能加强一下其他输出角色，提供更多的卡牌和强化，否则游戏初期爽感很强，但后期容易陷入公式化和重复的疲劳中。
it's a little light on the roguelike elements imo, but the card battling, character customization & overall production are first class. if you like System Crash, this is a no brainer.

This game has severe balance issues. With the right build, the starting offensive character can kill all the enemies in almost every encounter on turn 1 (With the only exceptions being one encounter with enemies that have a 3 damage cap and bosses that end your turn when a phase ends.) This is a game where you get extra rewards for clearing battles without taking health damage and the above build makes it happen every time. This is also a game where its really easy to get the same cards and equipment. For cards after each run your able to spend an account resource to make cards you had that run be available in all future runs (up to 5 cards) and there aren't too big a pool of cards anyways. For equipment, this game has equipment be divided into 4 different pack types with you choosing 1 of 2 equipment or some money when opening the pack. The build I mentioned only needs 1 specific equipment to work, so all you really need to do is save your money until you find a shop that sells the correct pack, then spam buy it until you get the required equipment. There is apparently also another character that can go infinite by themselves (I've only read someone on the steam discussions mention it, so not sure how its done or how much deckbuilding / equipment needed, but I can't be bothered to play more of this poorly balanced game to find out,)

This game rocks. A top tier deckbuilder with Cyberpunk theme and really cool mechanics and cards from the first run - unlike some other games the really cool stuff is not hidden behind meta progression. Also, the art being good surprised me. The humans are far the worse aspect of the art, so thar blond chick they used in the store is a real bad representation - vehicles, weapons and tech in general are really cool. This is what kept me from buying before the promo and rest assured it's not half as bad as it looks. I'm not sure about the replayability. Frankly, I finished my first run and came here to write this review to (maybe) help people to pull the trigger during the 25% off promo happening - but I feel it's totally worth the full price too.

很好的卡牌游戏，目前已经全成就了。开始刚玩的时候有一些难，但是属于越打越简单类型的，尤其无限模式解锁之后游戏难度大大降低。提个意见就是天赋界面确实不是很好找，打到总经理难度我才找到，还有就是增加更多玩法吧。期待后续更新更多探员和boss关卡

1、需要从10个角色共三个大职业中随意选择3个进行游戏，可以都是相同角色，自由度比较高，而且每个角色的能量是分开各打各的，所以需要相互配合就能打出无伤的战绩，比较考验出牌思路。 2、刻印功能保存卡牌，可以在下一次开始游戏的时候替换卡组里的初始卡，得到每个角色的关键卡或者过牌能力，就比较好启动整个卡组。 3、打赢之后是开箱子获得奖励，卡牌是6选2，装备是3选一，选了还得你放入卡组或者装备栏里才能生效，避免了臃肿。但是卡牌和装备战利品分了好几种，但是其实是没有区别的，除了卡牌后两个战利品有可能出升级过的卡牌，其他战利品里面的东西都是共用一个池子，一开始我还特意区分开，好记住什么类型的好出关键的物品，后面发现是随机出的，就觉得这个设计有点意义不明了。 4、因为存在卡组下限，刚开始玩发现除了几张个人专属卡，其他人的卡都是一个样就很难顶，那你设置这个区分度是干嘛的呢，而且一个角色的卡组里同名卡不能超过2张，不过打到解锁无限模式之后这个限制就不存在了。 5、只有一张卡的时候，如果那张卡需要丢弃卡牌才能发动，那就没法发动，不能白嫖，攻击力是负的情况下用翻倍，攻击力不会变回正的，而是两倍的负数，debuff说的回合开始敌人怎么怎么样，不是指敌方的回合开始，而是我方回合开始。这也是我发现的一些小毛病。 6、难度按照公司职位进行划分，一条爬到总裁的升职路，牛马一路爬完了。第一第二章共5个地图随机出现，boss也是随机，打boss成就不好完成。打了10几遍才第一次看到第二章的恒星大厦这幅图，后面发现只有战斗节点才会保存进度，不然从boss节点退出会回调到打boss前最后一个完成战斗的节点，重新进入的话有几率刷新敌人，这条定律适用所有的普通敌人，精英和boss，甚至问号事件也能改变，而且同一个剧情选择同样的选项，可能会出现不一样的的结果。 7、故事一开始疾风怒涛般展开，画风也比较赛博朋克，章节boss还有特殊动画，结果只有打boss前有几句剧情，后续嘎然而止，打完最终boss也没有丁点剧情，这就比较拉了。 8、角色我一直都是用的新手教程的战将，叛将，幻影，太好用了。 恶鬼面罩+超肾上腺+数据吸虫，这三个装备放在叛将身上就能永动，或者选个芬尼尔vx-3，配合卡牌交战，能一直杀下去，boss还没开始动就杀完了。然后事件的装备信仰灌注是个好东西，挂在幻影身上配合她的克隆体，嘎嘎猛，主要打法就是叛将利用多动清杂鱼，把攻击力拉高就能杀穿，战将的卡牌再动也能很好的帮叛将输出，阿特米西亚-3毒气，这张卡就是神卡，把对面的防御变成-3，输出一下子拉个一大截，前期就能安稳度过，而且不要怕自己也被挂上这个debuff，只要我杀的够快，对面就没法还击。如果到了解锁无限模式，战将就开始变态了，因为他的格挡每回合都能保留，天赋点最下面开局+12那个，配合2-3张钢铁意志，一张快速突袭和两张磁性射击，一回合就能把护甲拉到40-50，敌人又打不动，一下子就能秒boss，能拿到装备合成钢架就更猛了。

其实感觉有点想差评的，毕竟很多地方体验真的很差，就我目前找到的，我大概说一下 1.没有图鉴，别告诉我你这个分类不明，专属卡没区分的叫画廊的玩意叫图鉴，请问我该怎么知道哪些卡属于谁？我该怎么判断专属卡是谁的？而且你上面筛选的选项连个名称都没有，纯靠自己猜是什么意思呗，而且搜索框是真的意义不明，画廊还可以一直往空白后翻，有这么多页吗？ 2.你选人页面也太简陋了，没有天赋页，天赋强化只能进关卡才能知道有什么，没有初始卡组显示，没法判断这个角色具体定位是什么，或者说推断他的玩法是什么，也只能进关卡再看，甚至你选了人物之后，出了那个重置按钮直接下掉所有人以外，我不能单独下掉一个指定的人，我是真的迷惑，每个人物的名字也完全没有什么记忆点，而且除了选人页面和强化页面，其他的时候都不知道这人叫什么 3.部分词条也完全不明，手雷这个词条是什么意思？只是说明这个是手雷？穿刺是什么？什么伤害是穿刺？所有的射击？弹药是什么？命令是什么？辐射先锋那个激怒词条解释还是叫暴怒，这俩是一个东西？ 4.你第三章的boss有五轮战斗啊？第五轮还是dps检测器啊？第一次见到有回合制游戏boss战五连战无补给，清空buff，能量不回，只给抽卡就继续打的，哪怕我打过了也很憋屈，哪有这样的，还全是数值+机制 5.教程也模糊不清，物资机制到底是怎么算的？有物资时打boss有额外奖励吗？撤离时额外奖励到底是需要剩余1还是0，实际奖励减少是怎么判定的，都不知道 暂时问题就这么多，估计短时间内也不想打开了，玩的有点心累

《零异机动队》是一款规则独特的肉鸽卡牌游戏，核心玩法在于对三位队员的卡牌构筑和策略战斗，提供多样化的战斗策略。游戏优点包括新颖的战斗方式、可自由回头的地图设计、令人眼前一亮的BOSS动画和建模，以及充满科技感的美术风格。然而，游戏也存在一些缺点，如操作繁琐、可玩内容较少、奖励平衡差、部分角色超模等问题。总体来说，《零异机动队》是一款值得尝试的游戏，如果制作组能够持续更新和改进，相信会更加出色。
Despite some shortcomings, the good outweighs the bad, and the game delivers a fun cyberpunk themed burst of fun, before inevitably running out of new things to try. Recommended.
